# naming.interpreter.selector-and-property-index-currency

Kind: `native-observation`

## Problem statement

The interp command and child-interpreter command use different selector tables, and a configurable property selector can preserve its own index cache. Treating all index tables as one would validate a stale entry.

## Question

What selector inventory, original cache table identity and property warm/fresh/absent windows does the native interpreter probe retain?

## Conclusion

The captured interp/child and property windows keep each actual table and command result separate. Property setup refusals on older providers do not answer the later configurable-property cache question. Jim uses its own source and representation; C IndexRep observations are not donated to it.

## Scope

Only the original retained programs, capture windows and provider labels in the attached artifacts are covered. Version labels are original receipt metadata, not a fresh patchlevel query. Missing command/API doors and aborted processes stay distinct from successful guest completion. Source files/probes explain the observer protocol; no pinned engine implementation excerpt or executed Rust assertion is claimed. Different attempts and sources are retained separately, never treated as byte-identical duplicates.
